newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Inkombank says plans level two ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Inkombank says plans level two ADRs.

text.p: AB Inkombank, one of Russia's biggest banks, plans to issue level two American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) this year after a $100 million increase in capital, a senior bank official said on Thursday.
"New issues this year and next years are in our plans," vice-president Rafael Nagapetyants told Reuters.
The Central Bank permitted Inkombank to issue three percent of its capital in ADRs, share look-alikes which trade abroad.
Level two ADRs raise new capital and level one ADRs, which the company already has, do not.
Inkombank shares are very illiquid in Russia, like most Russian bank shares.
Nagapetyants said the bank had sold about 400,000 of 600,000 level one ADRs and planned to sell the rest after a road show in New York and Boston June 4-6.

He said Inkombank would increase its charter capital, currently $174 million by international accounting standards, by $100 million which would allow issuance of level two ADRs within its three percent ceiling.
But he did not give the volume or timing of the issue.
In January Inkombank became the first Russian bank to issue ADRs through brokerage C.A. Atlantic Securities Inc.
An ADR covers 15 underlying shares. It was unchanged on Thursday at 1600 GMT in Berlin at 25.50 marks from Wednesday's close.
The Bank of New York is acting as the depositary bank, ING-Bank Euroasia (Moscow) is the custodian and Inkombank acts as its own broker.
